synopsis: Complete platforms aim to cover scenarios, environments, sensors, vehicle motion and test execution, but usually still require separate machine models, controllers, asset pipelines or hardware benches; “complete” is relative [f15871, f8344, f15872]. The market is modular: road-vehicle tools are strong in sensors and scenarios, heavy-machine tools in terrain and hydraulics, and no single tool has public evidence of validating earth-moving-machine automatic braking across many site types and all-weather sensing [f13604, f194, f13071]. Off-road evidence includes MathWorks’ shipped excavator, backhoe and haul-truck examples in R2026b, the September 2025 Applied Intuition–Komatsu partnership, and Duality Falcon’s military applications, but independent heavy-machine automatic-braking validation was not found [f15878, f15882, f15889, f15921]. Integrated commercial stacks are considered faster for on-road-like elements but still need heavy-machine content; no time-to-first-useful-result benchmark or independent evidence of a universal integrated-versus-modular winner was found [f8750, f8749, f9359]. Nearly every commercial platform requires vendor quotations for budgeting; Falcon’s USD 20/month education license is a limited public-price exception, with its commercial price unavailable [f15922, f15888]. AURELION 26.2 was released on 15 July 2026, but listed AURELION/SIMPHERA evidence remains on-road only, and frame rates were not found for AURELION, CarMaker, DRIVE Sim/Omniverse, CARLA or MAVS [f8451, f8997, f4957].
